counted.claim: Transactions 3660108 and 3660106 were executed from device D009708, and transaction 3660107 from device D009709; both devices were new to the account and operated behind an anonymous proxy (IP_PROXY:ANONYMOUS).

Card C05061-K1 showed an abrupt run of three online product C transactions (3660106, 3660107, 3660108) totaling $2,189.02, deviating from its 34-transaction baseline of product W in person (27), product R online (6), and product H online (1) with zero product C purchases.

Two peer cards, C11543-K2 and C07212-K2, exhibited the identical scheme signature between 2017-01-07 and 2017-01-09 with online product C charges of $358-$1,113 behind anonymous proxies, using sequentially provisioned device IDs (D009706, D009707) and adjacent transaction IDs (3660115, 3660116, 3660122, 3660123, 3660124) directly preceding C05061-K1's devices (D009708, D009709) and transactions (3660106, 3660107, 3660108).

A concentrated burst of three high-value online transactions (3660106 for $850.28, 3660107 for $890.79, and 3660108 for $447.95) occurred over approximately 61 hours between 2017-01-12 and 2017-01-14, totaling $2,189.02.

Card C05061-K1 has three prior confirmed fraud cases, including CC-2420 for card_not_present_new_device involving unrecognized online purchases from an unfamiliar device, as well as CC-4210 and CC-2674.

Flagged transaction 3660108 and transaction 3660106 were billed in region 492, where the card has historical presence (3 prior transactions) and the region has a 0.0 fraud lift vs all transactions in the 7-day window.

first.section: Section 3a. A case is not a report
first.text: Section 3a. A case is not a report. Two different things, and the agent produces both. **A case** (`CREATE_CASE`) is the bank's internal record of an investigation. Open one whenever fraud probability reaches 0.30, whenever you request evidence, or whenever a customer disputes a charge. A case can be closed as fraud or as legitimate. It can be updated when new evidence arrives. It should be written into the graph so later investigations can find it: a case that names a merchant or a device becomes evidence for the next analyst. **A suspicious activity report** (`FILE_REPORT`) is a regulatory filing sent outside the bank. File one when fraud is confirmed or strongly suspected **and** at least one of these holds: exposure exceeds $1,000; the activity connects to a shared device profile, a shared region cluster, or another customer's fraud; the pattern is coordinated or undocumented (rule R9). A report always has a case behind it. Most cases never need a report. The report narrative must stand on its own: who, what, when, where, how, and why it is suspicious. Deciding correctly between ""case only"" and ""case plus report"" is part of the next-best-action score.

steps.detail: An investigation of card C05061-K1 was initiated following an analyst alert regarding coordinated losses across multiple cards. Between January 12 and January 14, 2017, three unauthorized online product C transactions (3660106, 3660107, 3660108) totaling $2,189.02 were conducted on the card. These transactions utilized new devices (D009708 and D009709) routing through an anonymous proxy, representing a complete deviation from the card's 34-transaction historical baseline. Graph analysis revealed that peer cards C11543-K2 and C07212-K2 experienced identical proxy-masked product C purchase runs using sequentially provisioned device IDs (D009706 through D009709). Card C05061-K1 also carries prior confirmed fraud history, including closed case CC-2420. Based on these findings, the activity was confirmed as card-not-present new-device fraud, resulting in a card block, case creation, and regulatory filing.
